title: VISTA Practical Workshop
text:
By the end of this practical you should be able to:

Load VISTA and its example RNA-seq data.
Inspect count data and sample metadata.
Prepare counts and metadata for VISTA.
Create and validate a VISTA object.
Understand where normalized expression, sample metadata, gene metadata, and DE results are stored.
Make QC, differential expression, and expression plots.
Run functional enrichment after checking DE results.
Export tables and plots.

2 Setup
Run this chunk first.

library(VISTA)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

Some later sections use optional Bioconductor packages. This helper lets us skip a section cleanly if a package is not installed.

has_pkg <- function(pkg) {
  requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)
}

text:
4 2. Understand the Inputs
The count table has one row per gene and one column per sample, plus a gene_id column.

colnames(count_data)

[1] "gene_id"    "SRR1039508" "SRR1039509" "SRR1039512" "SRR1039513"
[6] "SRR1039516" "SRR1039517" "SRR1039520" "SRR1039521"


The metadata has one row per sample. The sample_names column should match the count columns.

names(sample_metadata)

 [1] "SampleName"   "cell"         "dex"          "albut"        "Run"         
 [6] "avgLength"    "Experiment"   "Sample"       "BioSample"    "sample_names"
[11] "cond_long"    "cond_short"   "groups"      

sample_metadata$sample_names

[1] "SRR1039508" "SRR1039509" "SRR1039512" "SRR1039513" "SRR1039516"
[6] "SRR1039517" "SRR1039520" "SRR1039521"


Check the treatment column.

table(sample_metadata$dex)


  trt untrt 
    4     4 


For this workshop, we compare:

numerator: trt
denominator: untrt
group column: dex

In plain language: treated samples compared with untreated samples.

title: VISTA Practical Workshop
text:
5 3. Prepare Counts and Metadata
VISTA provides helper functions to standardize inputs before analysis.

prepared_counts <- read_vista_counts(
  count_data,
  format = "matrix",
  gene_id_column = "gene_id"
)


prepared_metadata <- read_vista_metadata(
  sample_metadata,
  sample_column = "sample_names"
)

Now match counts and metadata. This is one of the most important checks in RNA-seq analysis.

matched_inputs <- match_vista_inputs(
  counts = prepared_counts,
  sample_info = prepared_metadata,
  column_geneid = "gene_id",
  sample_column = "sample_names"
)

Inspect the matched output.

title: VISTA Practical Workshop
text:
6 4. Create a VISTA Object
Now we run differential expression and create a VISTA object.
For beginners, focus on these arguments:

counts: the gene count table.
sample_info: the sample metadata.
column_geneid: the gene ID column.
group_column: the metadata column defining groups.
group_numerator: the group in the numerator of the fold change.
group_denominator: the reference group.
method: the differential expression backend.


vista <- create_vista(
  counts = matched_inputs$counts,
  sample_info = matched_inputs$sample_info,
  column_geneid = matched_inputs$column_geneid,
  group_column = "dex",
  group_numerator = "trt",
  group_denominator = "untrt",
  method = "deseq2",
  min_counts = 10,
  min_replicates = 2,
  log2fc_cutoff = 1,
  pval_cutoff = 0.05,
  p_value_type = "padj"
)

Print the object.

vista

class: VISTA 
dim: 17199 8 
metadata(12): de_results de_summary ... design comparison
assays(1): norm_counts
rownames(17199): ENSG00000000003 ENSG00000000419 ... ENSG00000273487
  ENSG00000273488
rowData names(1): baseMean
colnames(8): SRR1039508 SRR1039509 ... SRR1039520 SRR1039521
colData names(14): SampleName cell ... sizeFactor sample_names

7 5. Validate the Object
Validation checks whether the VISTA object is internally consistent.

validate_vista(vista, level = "full")

8 6. Why the VISTA Object Matters
A VISTA object keeps several parts of the analysis together:

normalized expression values,
sample metadata,
gene metadata,
differential expression results,
analysis cutoffs,
color settings and plotting information.

This follows the same logic as Bioconductor’s SummarizedExperiment: data and metadata should stay synchronized.

9 7. Add Gene Annotations
The example data uses Ensembl gene IDs. For human-readable plots, gene symbols are useful.
This step uses org.Hs.eg.db. If the package is not installed, skip this section and continue with Ensembl IDs.

if (has_pkg("org.Hs.eg.db")) {
  vista <- set_rowdata(
    vista,
    orgdb = org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db,
    columns = c("SYMBOL", "GENENAME", "ENTREZID"),
    keytype = "ENSEMBL"
  )
}

title: VISTA Practical Workshop
text:
11 9. Quality Control Plots
QC plots help us check whether samples behave as expected.

11.1 Sample Correlation Heatmap

get_corr_heatmap(
  vista,
  viridis_direction = -1,
  show_corr_values = TRUE,
  label_size = 3
)










11.2 PCA Plot

get_pca_plot(
  vista,
  label = TRUE,
  shape_by = "cell"
)










11.3 MDS Plot

get_mds_plot(
  vista,
  label = TRUE,
  shape_by = "cell"
)










11.4 UMAP Plot
UMAP is optional and requires the uwot package.

if (has_pkg("uwot")) {
  get_umap_plot(
    vista,
    label = TRUE,
    shape_by = "cell"
  )
}

12.1 DEG Count Barplot

get_deg_count_barplot(vista)

    vista,

title: VISTA Practical Workshop
text:
13 11. Expression Plots for Selected Genes
Expression plots help us inspect individual genes or sets of genes.

selected_genes <- head(top_up, 4)
selected_genes

[1] "ENSG00000179593" "ENSG00000109906" "ENSG00000250978" "ENSG00000132518"



13.1 Expression Heatmap

if (has_pkg("ComplexHeatmap")) {
  get_expression_heatmap(
    vista,
    genes = c(head(top_up, 10), head(top_down, 10)),
    sample_group = c("untrt", "trt"),
    display_id = "SYMBOL",
    show_row_names = TRUE,
    summarise_replicates = FALSE,
    annotate_columns = c("dex", "cell")
  )
}










13.2 Barplot

get_expression_barplot(
  vista,
  genes = selected_genes,
  display_id = "SYMBOL",
  log_transform = TRUE,
  stats_group = TRUE
) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)










13.3 Boxplot

get_expression_boxplot(
  vista,
  genes = selected_genes,
  display_id = "SYMBOL",
  log_transform = TRUE,
  facet_by = "gene",
  stats_group = TRUE
) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)










13.4 Violin Plot

get_expression_violinplot(
  vista,
  genes = selected_genes,
  display_id = "SYMBOL",
  log_transform = TRUE,
  facet_by = "gene"
) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

title: VISTA Practical Workshop
text:
19 17. Pathway-Specific Heatmap
Use genes from enriched pathways and visualize their expression.

if (exists("msig_up") &&
    !is.null(msig_up$enrich) &&
    nrow(msig_up$enrich@result) > 0 &&
    has_pkg("ComplexHeatmap")) {

  get_pathway_heatmap(
    x = vista,
    enrichment = msig_up$enrich,
    sample_group = c("untrt", "trt"),
    top_n = 2,
    gene_mode = "union",
    max_genes = 50,
    value_transform = "zscore",
    display_id = "SYMBOL",
    annotate_columns = c("dex", "cell"),
    summarise_replicates = FALSE,
    show_row_names = FALSE
  )
}

title: VISTA Practical Workshop
text:
20 18. Export Results
Create an output directory.

dir.create("workshop_outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)

Save the main DE result table.

save_vista_data(
  vista,
  what = "comparison",
  sample_comparison = comp_name,
  file = file.path("workshop_outputs", "vista_de_results.csv")
)

Save a plot.

p <- get_ma_plot(
  vista,
  sample_comparison = comp_name,
  label_n = 10,
  display_id = "SYMBOL"
)

save_vista_plot(
  p,
  file = file.path("workshop_outputs", "ma_plot.png"),
  width = 8,
  height = 6
)

Export a bundle of standard assets.

export_vista_assets(
  vista,
  out_dir = "workshop_outputs/vista_assets",
  sample_comparison = comp_name,
  display_id = "SYMBOL"
)

Save the VISTA object for later.

saveRDS(vista, file = file.path("workshop_outputs", "airway_vista.rds"))

title: VISTA Practical Workshop
text:
21 19. Exercises
Try these after the main workflow runs. Start with the easy questions, then move to moderate and hard questions if you have time.

21.1 Easy Questions
These questions focus on reading objects, changing simple arguments, and understanding the output.

How many genes and samples are present in count_data?
Which column in sample_metadata stores the sample names used by VISTA?
How many samples are in each dex group?
What is the name of the comparison stored in comp_name?
How many genes are labelled Up, Down, and Other in de_table$regulation?
Change label_n in the MA plot from 10 to 20. What changes in the plot?
Make a PCA plot without sample labels by changing label = TRUE to label = FALSE.
Change the point size in the PCA plot. Which value makes the plot easiest to read?
Select the top 5 upregulated genes and print them.
Select the top 5 downregulated genes and print them.



21.2 Moderate Questions
These questions require modifying code and interpreting the result.

Create a barplot for the top 5 downregulated genes using get_expression_barplot().
Create a boxplot for the top 5 upregulated genes using get_expression_boxplot().
Change the expression heatmap so that it summarizes replicate groups instead of showing every sample.
Make the expression heatmap using only the top 10 upregulated genes.
Change the MA plot so that no genes are labelled. Which argument controls this?
Run MSigDB enrichment for downregulated genes instead of upregulated genes.
Make an enrichment plot for the downregulated MSigDB result.
Export the DE result table using a new filename, such as vista_de_results_updated.csv.
Save a PCA plot as a PNG file using save_vista_plot().
Compare the PCA and MDS plots. Do the samples group in a similar way?



21.3 Hard Questions
These questions are designed for deeper thinking, troubleshooting, and extending the workflow.

Change the differential expression cutoff in create_vista() from log2fc_cutoff = 1 to log2fc_cutoff = 0.5. How does the number of Up and Down genes change?
Change pval_cutoff = 0.05 to pval_cutoff = 0.01. How does this affect the DEG summary?
Re-run the workflow using method = "edger" instead of method = "deseq2". Are the top genes similar?
Add cell as a covariate in create_vista() using covariates = c("cell"). How does this change the results?
Try method = "both" and inspect the available DE result sources. What is the difference between using deseq2, edger, and consensus results?
Use set_de_source() to switch the active DE source if you created a multi-method VISTA object.
Run GO enrichment for downregulated genes and compare the top terms with the upregulated GO results.
Use get_pathway_genes() to extract genes from the top enriched pathway. Then make an expression heatmap for those genes.
Create a small report of your top biological interpretation: one sentence about the comparison, one sentence about the strongest DE genes, and one sentence about the top enriched pathway.
Think about reproducibility: which files would you save or share so someone else can repeat your analysis?

title: VISTA Practical Workshop
text:
22 20. Key Takeaways

Always inspect data before analysis.
Sample names in counts and metadata must match.
A VISTA object keeps expression, metadata, annotations, and results together.
QC plots should be checked before interpretation.
Functional analysis should be run after DE results and gene IDs are understood.
Exported tables and plots make the analysis easier to share and reproduce.
